Menu

A list of actions on one thing, opened from a button.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For three or more actions on one item that do not all fit beside it, such as the actions on a task or a run.
  • For the less common actions of a view, behind a button that names what they act on.

When not to use it

  • For one or two actions. Show them as buttons.
  • For the main action of a view. Show it as the primary button.
  • To choose a value in a form. Use a select.
  • To move between views. Use links, a tab bar or a sidebar.
  • For content that is not a list of actions. Use a popover.

Variants

item
The default item, with no modifier class. An optional ds-menu__icon comes before its text.
danger item ds-menu__item--danger
An item that deletes or cannot be undone. It is last, below a ds-menu__divider, and its label names what is lost.

Accessibility

  • Give the menu the popover attribute, an id, role="menu" and an aria-label. Give the button popovertarget with that id and aria-haspopup="menu". The browser opens and closes the menu, sets aria-expanded on the button, closes on Escape and on a press outside, and returns focus to the button.
  • Put the menu straight after its button in the markup. Each item is a button with type="button", role="menuitem" and the class ds-menu__item. Its label is a verb and what it acts on. An icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true".
  • A section is a div with role="group", the class ds-menu__section and aria-labelledby pointing at its ds-menu__label, which carries role="presentation". A divider is an hr with ds-menu__divider.
  • An unavailable item carries aria-disabled="true", so it stays in the arrow-key order and a screen reader can find it, and the app ignores presses on it. The behaviours module ignores Enter and Space on it. Say why in its label when the reason is not obvious.
  • Without script the menu still works: Tab moves through the items and Enter or Space activates one. The rest of the keyboard is script, as a roving focus. Wrap the button and the menu in the ds-menu element from behaviors/menu.js, or do the same in the app: when the menu opens (its toggle event), move focus to the first item, and give every item tabindex="-1" except the one that has focus. Down and Up move focus to the next and the previous item and wrap at the ends, Home and End go to the first and the last, and a letter key goes to the next item that starts with it. Tab closes the menu with hidePopover(), and focus moves on from the button. Escape stays the browser's.
  • One ds-menu element may wrap several menus, such as a list whose rows each end in a context menu. A menu shown as a manual popover is one the app keeps open itself, and the element moves no focus when it opens.
  • After an item's action runs, the app closes the menu with hidePopover(), and focus returns to the button.
  • Where the browser supports CSS anchor positioning the menu hangs below its button and flips at the edge of the screen. Elsewhere it sits centred at the bottom of the screen. To open it from script, call showPopover({ source: button }).
